notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to open the source pages (Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Augustine on New Advent, the NET Bible notes and Precept Austin) went over the tool's usage limit. After that, no more tool calls were allowed this turn, so I didn't read any pages.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for each point. Without having read anything, I have nothing I can honestly cite. I haven't filled the gap from my own knowledge, since that would break your rules.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll fetch these pages one at a time to stay under the limit:
- **Traditional, verse by verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-53/, and the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Barnes commentaries on Psalms 53 at biblehub.com/commentaries/
- **Spurgeon:** his *Treasury of David* on Psalm 53, at spurgeon.org or studylight.org
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes, especially on "Mahalath," "Maskil," and how verse 5 differs from Psalm 14:5–6
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's sermon on this psalm at newadvent.org. His older Bible numbered it Psalm 52, so the page is likely newadvent.org/fathers/1801052.htm.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Reformed, Wesleyan and Lutheran sources on verses 1–3, since Paul quotes those lines in Romans 3:10–12 and they bear on what each tradition teaches about how deeply sin affects people.
